question: Which company was responsible for laying the railway lines in Eastern India during the colonial period?

options.text: Bombay Baroda and Central India Railway

solution:
The correct answer is __**East Indian Railway Company**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **The East Indian Railway Company (EIR) **was responsible for laying the railway lines in Eastern India during the colonial period.
 
• The EIR was incorporated in **1845 **and its first railway line, between Howrah and Hooghly, was opened in 1854. The EIR went on to build a network of railways that covered much of Eastern India, including Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, and West Bengal.
 
• The EIR was a private company, but it received financial assistance from the British government.
 
• The company was also given a monopoly on railway construction in its area of operation.
 
• This monopoly gave the EIR a significant advantage over its competitors and helped it to become the largest railway company in India.
 
• The EIR played a major role in the economic development of Eastern India. The railways helped to improve transportation links and to facilitate trade and commerce.
 
• The EIR was nationalized in 1950 and became part of the Indian Railways.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Madras Railway **was responsible for laying the railway lines in **Southern India during the colonial period. **
 
• The Madras Railway was incorporated in **1845 **and its first railway line, between **Royapuram and Vepery, was opened in 1856. **
 
• The Madras Railway went on to build a network of railways that covered much of **Southern India, including Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka.**
